diagnostic_evidence.quote: A strictly monotonically increasing and differentiable function $\sigma: \R \to \R$ is called \emph{sigmoidal} if it satisfies

issues.failure_explanation: The definition requires limits 1 at +infinity and 0 at -infinity, but tanh tends to +1 and -1 and arctan to +pi/2 and -pi/2, so neither is sigmoidal as defined. The text thus recommends activations that fail its own definition, and the approximation theorems, which assume a sigmoidal activation 'as defined in def:sigm_act', do not literally cover them.

failure_location.quote: For examples, the logistic sigmoid function, the hyperbolic tangens and the arctangens are sigmoidial.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Qualify the sentence by requiring affine rescaling of tanh and arctan to limits 0 and 1 before use (or rescale them in the definition).
issues.overall_effect: The stated admissible activation class is wrong; th:function apx, th:functional apx and th:operatorapx as phrased exclude tanh and arctan used without rescaling.
issues.title: Named sigmoidal examples violate the paper's own definition
issues.why_classification: A one-line qualification preserves every claim for the named activations once rescaled; no argument, rate or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The branch term sums over l but evaluates x at the single point s_j, so it collapses to sigma(wbar_{j,k} x(s_j)+theta_{j,k}); the operator has the form sum_j G_j(x(s_j)) tau_j(t) with each G_j a function of one scalar. Such maps cannot approximate operators whose output coefficients depend on several input values, e.g. x -> x(s_1)x(s_2)psi(t), whose second mixed difference in the two values is nonzero while vanishing for any representation with coefficients depending on one value each. Hence the universality asserted for 'F_n from eq:deeponet' is false for the class as defined. The architecture is also incompatible with eq:nldeep (which uses x(s_l)) and with the parameter count of th:operatorapx (points s_l listed, but m coordinates charged per j).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-index the sensor points to s_l inside the branch sum as in eq:nldeep, and adjust the coefficient list eq:D and the parameter count in th:operatorapx accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The universal approximation claims of th:operatorapx and th:l2 operator apx fail for the defined class, and the identification of the operator built in eq:nldeep with a special case of eq:deeponet fails.
issues.title: Neural-operator branch net is degenerate in the sensor index
issues.why_classification: A local index repair restores the DeepONet structure and every approximation claim, with no change to any argument or rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which are the compact subsets of $\X$ and $\Y$, respectively

issues.failure_explanation: The display asserts one fixed coefficient set approximating the functionals x -> inner(x, ulx^(l)) uniformly for all x in X. Since sigma is bounded (limits 0 and 1) and the coefficients are fixed, every branch output is bounded, whereas the inner product with a fixed element is an unbounded linear functional on the infinite-dimensional space X; uniform approximation on all of X is impossible. The companion statement that the spans X_N and Y_N 'are the compact subsets of X and Y' is likewise false: they are unbounded linear subspaces.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the approximation claim of eq:nldeep to a fixed bounded subset of X (e.g. the ball used in cor:rate) and delete the compactness assertion on the spans.
issues.overall_effect: eq:nldeep does not define a uniform surrogate on X; only bounded-set statements such as eq:qn on a ball can hold.
issues.title: Uniform neural-network approximation claimed on all of the image space
issues.why_classification: Restricting the quantifier is a short local edit that preserves the construction and all later rates, which are only claimed on bounded sets anyway.

issues.failure_explanation: From eq:expansion, F_N^# = F P_N^X with P_N^X the projector in X, so ||F x - F_N^# x|| = ||F(I-P_N^X)x||; this is not bounded by nu_N = ||(I-P_N)F||, where P_N projects in Y. For instance on R^2 with F = [[1,1],[0,eps]] and the single training image e_1, one gets ||F e_2 - F_N^# e_2|| = sqrt(1+eps^2) while ||(I-P_N)F|| = eps. The bound also omits the factor ||x|| needed to hold on the ball B_rho(xdagger). The added claim that nu_N tends to 0 'when F is compact' is false as well: it requires nestedness and density of the spaces Y_N, which arbitrary training sets do not provide.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace nu_N by sup over the ball of ||F(I-P_N^X)x|| (projection in X), and add the hypothesis that the sample spans are nested with dense union, under which compactness of F yields convergence to zero.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate eq:estimate, the bound rho_n <= nu_N + N q(N) r(N), the approximation rate attributed to F_N^# in ta:operators, and the second rate expression of th:linear become unreliable.
issues.title: Operator-approximation bound uses the wrong projector
issues.why_classification: The key quantity must be redefined and a new hypothesis plus a short compactness argument are needed to retain the convergence claim; the rate form survives, so no new proof architecture is required.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing Ftilde_n x = sum_l atilde_l(x) ytilde^(l) with |a_l - atilde_l| <= q(N) and ||y^(l) - ytilde^(l)|| <= r(N), the identity a_l y^(l) - atilde_l ytilde^(l) = (a_l-atilde_l)(y^(l)-ytilde^(l)) + (a_l-atilde_l) ytilde^(l) + atilde_l (y^(l)-ytilde^(l)) produces one term of size q(N)r(N) and two terms of size q(N) and r(N), multiplied by ||ytilde^(l)|| and |atilde_l(x)| which the hypotheses do not bound. The second term of eq:estimate is therefore of order N(M r(N) + A q(N)), not N q(N) r(N); the rate O(N^{-1-p/2}) derived from eq:estNqr does not follow (with q(N)=N^{-2} and r(N)=O(N_j^{-1/2}) the corrected bound converges only if N_j grows faster than N^2).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound all three error terms, adding uniform bounds on ||ytilde^(l)||_Y and |inner(x, ulx^(l))| on the ball, and re-derive the coupling between N and N_j with the resulting N(M r(N) + A q(N)) term.
issues.overall_effect: The estimate eq:estimate, the bound rho_n <= nu_N + N q(N) r(N), the rate O(N^{-1-p/2}), the claim that the network-error term is 'of less importance', and the second expression of th:linear are unsupported.
issues.title: Network approximation errors combined as a product instead of a sum
issues.why_classification: The estimate must be redone with extra bounds and the derived parameter coupling is reoptimized and materially different, but the corollary's structure and the O(sqrt(delta)+sqrt(rho_n)) rates survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We choose the coefficients $(\ol{w}_{k}^{(\ell)},\ol{\theta}_{k}^{(\ell)})$ such that \autoref{eq:expl2} holds
Let us assume that $\x$ and $\ulx^{(\ell)}$ are bounded between $(0,1)$.

issues.failure_explanation: eq:expl2 requires one fixed pair (w,theta) with sigma^{-1}(x(t_k) ulx(t_k)) = w x(t_k) + theta; the left-hand side is not affine in the scalar x(t_k) (for the logistic link it is log(c v/(1-c v))), so eq:expl-eq:expl2 can hold for at most one value of x(t_k) and not for all x as eq:qn demands. In addition the ball B_rho(xdagger) in L^2(0,1) contains functions that are not twice differentiable, not defined pointwise and not bounded by 1, so neither the trapezoidal rule, nor the values x(t_k), nor the sigma^{-1} construction are available there. Hence the claimed rate q(N)=N^{-2} (obtained by setting N_k = N) is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the single-unit realization by a genuine sigmoidal approximation of the products x(t_k) ulx(t_k) on the bounded range of the inputs (with enough units and a proved rate), state the smoothness and boundedness hypotheses on x, and justify the identification N_k = N.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit coefficient construction, the rate q(N)=N^{-2}, the bound eq:estNqr and the derived rate O(N^{-1-p/2}) are unsupported, so cor:rate has no verified instance.
issues.title: Branch-net coefficients cannot realize the quadrature products
issues.why_classification: The construction and its rate must be replaced by a nontrivial approximation argument with input hypotheses, but the framework of cor:rate and the rates expressed in q and r survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: suppose that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$
which are the compact subsets of $\X$ and $\Y$, respectively
Therefore, by the Arzel\`a-Ascoli theorem, this subset is compact in $C(\ol{\Omega_\X})$.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, 'compact in V' only requires every sequence of U to have a subsequence converging to some element of V, not of U; this is relative compactness and is strictly weaker than compactness. The hypotheses of th:functional apx and th:operatorapx ('the domain is compact in C(overline(Omega_X))') therefore do not supply the genuinely compact domains assumed in the cited results, whereas under the correct definition the same hypotheses would fail for the intended applications (bounded balls in Sobolev spaces are only relatively compact in C). The statement that the spans X_N, Y_N 'are the compact subsets of X and Y' is false under either reading.

failure_location.quote: We say that $\U$ is compact in $\V$ if every sequence in $\U$ has a subsequence that converges in the $\norms{\cdot}_V$-norm to an element in $\V$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define compactness correctly (subsequential limits inside U) and phrase the hypotheses of th:functional apx and th:operatorapx as relative compactness of the domain together with continuity on its closure; delete the compactness claim on the spans.
issues.overall_effect: Every use of 'compact' (the hypotheses of th:functional apx and th:operatorapx, the claim on X_N and Y_N, the Arzela-Ascoli step of th:l2 operator apx) is ambiguous and, read literally, weaker than what the invoked results require.
issues.title: Compactness is defined as relative compactness
issues.why_classification: Fixing the definition and the two hypothesis wordings is local and keeps every intended application and rate; no new argument or construction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be a continuous operator with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology, and assume that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$

The proof follow easily from the Rellich-Kondrachov theorem (see \cite[Theorem 6.2]{Ada75}), which states that the embedding $H^s(\Omega_\X) \hookrightarrow C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$ is compact for $s > \frac{m}{2}$, and from \cite[Theorem 4 \& Theorem 5]{TiaHon95}.

issues.failure_explanation: Continuity for the H^s-topology does not imply continuity for the sup-norm topology, yet every approximant sum_k C_k sigma(sum_l w_{k,l} x(s_l)+theta_k) is sup-norm continuous and so cannot uniformly approximate functionals that are only H^s-continuous on a C-compact domain. Counterexample: on Omega_X=(0,1) take x_n(t)=n^{-s} sin(2 pi n t) (bounded in H^s, sup-norm tending to 0), D={x_n} union {0}, F(0)=0, F(x_n)=1. F is H^s-continuous on D (no nontrivial sequence of D converges in H^s) and D is compact in C, but no such network approximates F uniformly within 1/2, since network values converge along x_n -> 0 while those of F do not. The claimed reduction ('follows easily from Rellich-Kondrachov ... and from TiaHon95') thus applies the cited theorems outside their hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: be a continuous functional with respect to the $(H^s(\Omega_\X),\norms{\cdot}_{H^s})$-topology, and suppose that the domain $\dom{F}$ is compact in $C(\overline{\Omega_\X})$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add sup-norm continuity of F on D(F) (automatic for the smoothing forward operators of the examples) or require D(F) to be compact in the H^s-norm, and adjust the reduction accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: th:functional apx and th:operatorapx are false as stated; the claimed extension of neural-operator approximation to Sobolev-space domains holds only for functionals and operators continuous for the sup-norm topology on the domain (or for domains compact in H^s).
issues.title: Sobolev-space approximation theorems assume continuity in the wrong topology
issues.why_classification: The repair is a hypothesis change that withdraws part of the claimed function or domain class and needs a short closure argument, but leaves a recognizably comparable approximation result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For a function $\x \in L^2(\Omega_\X)$, which is extended by zero outside of $\Omega_\X \subseteq \R^m$

issues.failure_explanation: With the zero extension fixed in def:mollifier, the estimate ||x_xi - x||_{H^s} <= C xi^{k-s} ||x||_{H^k} fails at the boundary: for x identically 1 on Omega_X=(0,1) (an element of H^k for every k) one gets x_xi(t) = integral from -1 to t/xi of phi(u) du, which tends to 1/2 as t -> 0+, so ||x_xi - x||_{L^2} is of order sqrt(xi) instead of O(xi^2) for k=2, s=0. The quoted mollifier estimates apply to functions on R^m (or to bounded extensions) and not to zero-extended Sobolev functions whose traces do not vanish; the cited results are used outside their hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: For all $s \leq k$ and $\x \in H^k(\Omega_\X)$, $$\norms{\x_\xi-\x}_{H^s} \leq C\xi^{k-s}\norms{\x}_{H^k} = \mathcal{O}(\xi^{k-s})\;.$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Mollify a bounded extension of x instead of its zero extension (or restrict the estimate to functions with vanishing boundary traces and treat the boundary layer separately).
issues.overall_effect: The rates ||xdagger_xi - xdagger||_{L^2} = O(xi^2) and ||x_xi - x||_{L^2} = O(xi^2) used for the c-example are false as stated, and the mollification term of eq:xi degrades from order xi to a sqrt(xi)-type rate if the zero extension is kept.
issues.title: Mollification rate is false for the zero extension
issues.why_classification: Replacing the zero extension by a standard bounded extension operator is a local change of def:mollifier that restores all stated rates and guarantees, without a new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the subset $\{\x_\xi : \x \in \mathcal{B}_{\tt r}(\x^*) \} \subseteq \mathcal{B}_{\tt r}(\x^*) \cap \X_\xi$ is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous

issues.failure_explanation: Frechet differentiability only yields ||F[x]-F[x_xi]|| <= c ||x - x_xi||_{L^2}, and the supremum of ||x-x_xi||_{L^2} over an L^2-ball never tends to zero: for any xi and radius r, the element x = x* + r h with h oscillating at frequency much larger than 1/xi satisfies ||x - x_xi|| >= r - o(1), since ||h_xi|| -> 0 for such h. The asserted bound 'locally uniformly within an L^2-neighborhood' is therefore an invalid inference. Moreover the conclusion cannot hold on balls whose radius is independent of epsilon: for F the identity (admissible, F'=I, L=0) the map x -> F_n[x_xi] is determined by the finitely many linear functionals x -> x_xi(s_j) = inner(x, phi_xi(.-s_j)), whose common kernel is infinite-dimensional, so two ball points at distance 2r share the same F_n-value and force epsilon >= r.

failure_location.quote: it follows that there exists a $\xi > 0$ such that the following holds locally uniformly within an $L^2(\Omega_\X)$-neighborhood $\mathcal{B}_{\tt r}(\x^*)$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified for the stated locally-uniform-in-L2 claim; at minimum, a repair must replace L2-neighborhoods by input sets carrying a uniform mollification bound (for example bounded subsets of a Sobolev space or a compact class of inputs) and restate the guarantee accordingly, which removes the advertised L2 regime.
issues.overall_effect: eq:deeponeterror_l2 delivers at best a ball whose radius shrinks with epsilon; the c-example's coupling rho_{n xi} ~ delta on a fixed neighborhood, its rate O(sqrt(delta)+xi) of eq:xi, and the advertised extension of neural-operator approximation to Lebesgue spaces are unsupported.
issues.title: Local uniform mollification bound in L2 is an invalid inference
issues.why_classification: The central quantifier (uniformity on L2-balls of fixed radius) is false for admissible operators, so every complete resolution changes the guarantee type and excludes the Lebesgue-space regime that Section 6 exists to cover.
